setup: Hang from the bar, overhand grip
Let your shoulders rise toward your ears
execution: Arms stay straight the whole time
Your body rises a few centimetres
Lower slowly back to a full hang

notes: The movement is small; only the shoulder blades move.
Step down onto a box or bench rather than dropping from the bar.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain in the shoulder that builds during the set
Numbness or tingling in the hands

regressions.name: Feet-supported scap pull-up

regressions.name: Assisted pull-up
regressions.reason: Do the same shoulder-blade pull with machine assistance.

progressions.name: Hold at the top
progressions.reason: A 5–10 second hold with the shoulder blades down.

progressions.name: Pull-up
progressions.reason: Continue from the shoulder-blade pull into a full pull-up.

substitutions.reason: Lats with straight arms on a cable; loadable.

substitutions.name: Dead hang

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at shoulder height, figure facing right, hanging from a bar. The change is small, so frame the upper body large enough that the shoulders and the body's rise are clear.

keyPositions.label: Hang
keyPositions.describe: Hanging from the bar with straight arms, shoulders shrugged up toward the ears, body relaxed and still.

keyPositions.label: Pulled down
keyPositions.describe: Arms still straight. Shoulders drawn down away from the ears and slightly back; the body has risen a few centimetres. Chest slightly lifted.

ikHints: Elbows stay straight in every frame
emphasise: Shoulders move down away from the ears
